channel.title: Companies on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Companies on Best of AI

item.title: Xiaomi
item.description: Xiaomi has built a serious open model family, MiMo, to run across its phones, cars and smart home products. MiMo-V2-Pro and Omni, aimed at agents and multimodal use, launched in March 2026. MiMo-V2.5 and V2.5-Pro followed on April 28 under the MIT license. MiMo-V2.6-Pro, Flash and a 9B model arrived on September 21, 2026 with open weights, training code and reinforcement learning environments. Flash is a mixture-of-experts model with 309 billion total parameters and 15 billion active, and Pro scored 46 on Artificial Analysis’s Intelligence Index, the highest for an open-weight model there at launch.

item.title: Ant Group
item.description: Ant Group, the company behind Alipay, runs the inclusionAI lab, which publishes the Ling and Ring open-weight models. Ling is the general model line and Ring the reasoning line. In February 2026 it released Ling-2.5-1T and Ring-2.5-1T, the latter described as the first hybrid linear-architecture thinking model. Ling-2.6-1T, built for agents and tool use, followed on April 30, and Ring-2.6-1T, a trillion-parameter MoE reasoning model under the MIT license, around May 8 to 14.

item.title: 01.AI
item.description:
01.AI, founded by Kai-Fu Lee, built the open Yi models, which were strong on release in 2023 and 2024 but have not kept pace with newer Chinese labs. The company has shifted toward enterprise work. Its Number One Officer project has Lee acting as a client’s chief AI strategy officer, and Wanzhi, launched in March 2025, is a platform for deploying AI apps inside companies.

Lee told LatePost the company is dismantling its offshore structure to prepare for an IPO, with quarterly profit targeted by 2027. We could not confirm when he said it. A 2026 Fudan listing calls Lee CEO of Lingyi Wanwu, which looks like the company’s Chinese-facing name, though sources do not state that outright.

item.title: Adobe
item.description:
Adobe builds AI into the apps its customers already use. Firefly is its family of image, video, vector and audio models, trained on licensed and Adobe Stock content, which Adobe pitches as safer for commercial work. Firefly runs on a credit system, and usage inside Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and Express draws from the same pool.

In April 2026 Adobe launched the Firefly AI Assistant, which can operate across Creative Cloud apps from a single prompt. Asking it to prepare a social campaign, for example, can involve Photoshop, Premiere and Express in sequence. By June it was available in Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator, InDesign and Frame.io. Adobe has said it is exploring working with third-party models, and some outlets reported Claude support, though Adobe’s own wording was more cautious.

item.title: AI21 Labs
item.description:
AI21 Labs, based in Tel Aviv, makes the Jamba models, which combine Mamba state-space layers with transformer layers to handle long inputs more cheaply. It also sells Maestro, an agent platform, and earlier built the Jurassic models. NVIDIA and Google backed a $300 million round in May 2025, and AI21 has raised about $626 million across nine rounds.

In late December 2025, Calcalist reported that NVIDIA was in advanced talks to buy AI21 for $2 billion to $3 billion, possibly folding Maestro into NVIDIA AI Enterprise, with some coverage calling it mainly an acquihire of about 200 staff. Neither company confirmed a deal. One secondary post says it did not go ahead and that Nebius then looked at buying AI21, but that claim has a single undated source.

item.title: Aleph Alpha
item.description:
Aleph Alpha, based in Heidelberg, built models for European governments and enterprises that want AI hosted outside US and Chinese providers. Its Luminous and Pharia models were aimed at that audience.

In April 2026 it agreed to merge with Cohere, with Cohere’s shareholders holding about 90 percent of the combined company and Aleph Alpha’s holders 10 percent. Schwarz Group, an Aleph Alpha investor, said it would put $600 million into Cohere’s Series E. The deal needs antitrust approval and we could not confirm that it has closed. One source puts the combined valuation near $20 billion. Cohere describes the pairing as a transatlantic sovereign AI company.

item.title: Alibaba
item.description: Alibaba’s AI efforts run through Qwen, one of the most widely used open model families in the world. Qwen3.8 is the current generation. The company announced it in July 2026, and Qwen3.8-Max became generally available on August 3 as a mixture-of-experts model with 2.4 trillion total parameters, about 95 billion active per query and a 1 million token context window. Open weights followed in August, along with a smaller dense 27B vision-language model under Apache 2.0.

item.title: Allen Institute for AI
item.description:
Ai2 is a nonprofit that releases fully open models, meaning weights, data and training code. Olmo 3, released in November 2025 in 7B and 32B sizes, was its first generation to include a reasoning model, with Base, Think, Instruct and RL Zero versions, and Olmo 3.1 extended the reinforcement learning. Molmo 2, from December 2025, is an open vision-language model with video understanding, pointing and tracking.

Ai2’s news page lists Olmo Hybrid in March 2026, a 7B model that combines transformer attention with linear RNN layers, and MolmoPoint, a pointing architecture. One aggregator dates an Olmo-core 3 training stack for mixture-of-experts models to October 2026, which we could not confirm. Ai2 also takes part in the NSF-backed OMAI project. Some hosted endpoints for older Olmo and Molmo models were retired in March 2026.

item.title: Amazon
item.description:
Amazon’s AI work mostly runs through AWS. Bedrock lets customers call models from Anthropic, Meta, Mistral and others through one API, and Amazon’s own Nova family sits alongside them. Nova 2 is the current generation, with Pro handling text, images, video and speech, and Sonic covering voice. Bedrock AgentCore is the platform AWS sells for building and running production agents, with newer features for memory and policy controls.

Consumer AI centers on Alexa+, the rebuilt assistant that uses Nova and Anthropic models and is now available to US customers. For developers, Kiro is Amazon’s agentic coding environment, and Amazon Q covers coding help and business questions.

item.title: AMD
item.description: AMD’s AI business centers on the Instinct accelerators and the ROCm software stack. In October 2025 OpenAI agreed to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs across several generations, starting with 1 gigawatt in 2026, and received a warrant for up to 160 million AMD shares that vest as deployment and share-price milestones are met. Oracle plans 50,000 MI450 GPUs in a supercluster built on AMD’s Helios rack. We found no confirmation that OpenAI has finished a full MI450 deployment.

item.title: Anthropic
item.description:
Anthropic builds Claude, a model family sold in four tiers: Fable, Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku. The 5.5 generation is current, with Haiku 5.5 arriving on October 7, 2026, after Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 in September. Fable 5.1 is the top general-access model. Mythos is a separate, restricted class offered only to approved organizations, mostly in cybersecurity and life sciences.

The products around the models have grown quickly. Claude Code, the command-line coding agent, reached general availability in May 2025. Cowork brings the same file and task automation to people who do not write code, and Claude Design, launched on April 17, 2026, produces visuals and prototypes. Claude Code Security, introduced in February 2026, scans codebases for vulnerabilities.

item.title: Anysphere
item.description:
Cursor is an AI code editor, and the company behind it, Anysphere, has become one of the most valuable AI startups. Its own model, Composer, launched in November 2025 and Composer 2.5 followed in May 2026. The editor lets developers run several agents at once and choose models from different labs.

Ownership changed in 2026. In April, xAI reportedly paid for exclusive collaboration rights with an option to buy Cursor for $60 billion, ahead of a planned $2 billion raise at about $50 billion. On June 16, SpaceX exercised the option in an all-stock deal valued at $60 billion, expected to close in the third quarter. A model built with xAI is expected to ship in both Cursor and Grok Build.

item.title: Apple
item.description:
Apple’s AI strategy is built around on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute. Apple Intelligence runs a small foundation model on the device and sends heavier requests to Apple’s own servers. The Foundation Models framework lets third-party apps use the on-device model, and the current version also supports models from other providers.

The biggest change is Siri. Apple and Google agreed to a multi-year deal in which the next generation of Apple Foundation Models is built on Gemini. At WWDC on June 8, 2026, Apple showed Siri AI for iOS 27, iPadOS 27 and macOS 27, with a public release planned for the fall. Reports say it will not launch at first in the EU or China. A figure of about $1 billion a year for the deal circulates in the press but is unconfirmed.

item.title: AssemblyAI
item.description: AssemblyAI sells speech recognition and audio intelligence by API. Universal-3 Pro, launched around February 4, 2026, lets developers add a text prompt alongside audio to shape the transcript. A streaming version followed in early March for voice agents. The company says it has a lower missed-entity rate than rivals in hard audio, which is a vendor benchmark. Its site now promotes Universal-3.5 Pro, listed on OpenRouter on September 22, 2026, and we found no detailed coverage of how it differs.

item.title: Baichuan AI
item.description: Baichuan changed direction toward medicine. On January 13, 2026 it open-sourced Baichuan-M3, a medical model that CEO Wang Xiaochuan presented as able to run a consultation like a doctor. The company says it beat OpenAI’s GPT-5.2 on HealthBench and HealthBench Hard, with a score of 65.1 on the former, and that about 80 percent of its compute goes to reinforcement learning. Nine days later it released M3 Plus, which cut the reported hallucination rate from 3.5 to 2.6 percent and API prices by 70 percent. It also offers the model free by API to Chinese healthcare institutions.

item.title: Baidu
item.description:
Baidu’s AI work revolves around Ernie. ERNIE 5.0 was unveiled in November 2025 as a natively multimodal model and reached final release in early 2026. ERNIE 5.1 followed on May 9, 2026 as a closed-weight sparse mixture-of-experts model with a 128K token context window. Baidu has not published a parameter count. Earlier versions, Ernie 4.0 and 4.5, are in our model list.

Baidu designs its own chips under the Kunlun name. The roadmap has the M100 for inference in 2026 and the M300 for training very large multimodal models in 2027, and it reportedly plans to spin off the chip unit, Kunlunxin, and list it in Hong Kong. Baidu says a Kunlunxin cluster helped train part of the ERNIE 5.1 series.

item.title: Black Forest Labs
item.description:
Black Forest Labs was started by researchers who built the original Stable Diffusion, and its FLUX models are some of the most widely used image generators. The lineup includes FLUX.1, FLUX.1 Kontext for editing and FLUX.2, which arrived days before a $300 million Series B in December 2025 at a $3.25 billion valuation. AMP and Salesforce Ventures led, with NVIDIA, a16z and General Catalyst reported among participants.

The Financial Times has reported talks on a new round that could value the company at up to $4 billion, but we found no confirmation that it closed. Total funding figures from trackers range from about $450 million to $576 million.

item.title: ByteDance
item.description:
ByteDance’s AI efforts sit under Seed, and the consumer face is Doubao, which Quest Mobile counts at about 155 million weekly active users in China. Doubao-Seed-2.0 launched on February 14, 2026, with a Pro model positioned against GPT-5.2 and Gemini 3 Pro for long reasoning and agent tasks.

Seedance 2.0, a video generation model, debuted on February 12 and moved quickly into the market: it is available in Doubao, Jimeng and Volcano Engine, ByteDance’s cloud, and the API opened to the public in April. It reached overseas users through CapCut with copyright safeguards. Seedream handles images.

item.title: Canva
item.description:
Canva introduced Canva AI 2.0 in research preview in May 2026, which it calls its biggest product change since launching in 2013. You can design by conversation, have the AI edit across a project, and keep a persistent memory of your brand and preferences. Canva describes it as a “creative OS” tying together six connected workflows. Magic Studio, the earlier set of image, writing and video tools, remains underneath.

The company has also been buying creative software. Affinity, the design suite Canva acquired in 2024, was relaunched as a free app in late 2025 and reportedly gained a Claude integration in 2026. Canva also acquired the motion-design tool Cavalry and made it free, plus several smaller companies including MangoAI and Simtheory. In August 2026 designs could be created inside Google Gemini and AI Search.

item.title: Cartesia
item.description:
Cartesia makes low-latency voice models built on state space architectures, which the founders helped develop. Sonic-3, announced in October 2025, supports 42 languages with model latency near 90 milliseconds, though one post cites 190 milliseconds end to end. A $100 million round was reported with it, from NVIDIA and others, but funding totals differ by source, from $64 million for an earlier Series A to $191 million overall.

2026 items on aggregator pages include Mamba-3, an inference-first architecture in March, and Ink-2, a speech-to-text model that reportedly topped Artificial Analysis’s new STT leaderboard in May. We found no confirmed 2026 funding round and no primary sources for those two.

item.title: Cerebras Systems
item.description:
Cerebras builds wafer-scale processors and sells their speed for inference. It went public on Nasdaq in mid-May 2026 under CBRS, the largest US tech IPO since Snowflake. Reports disagree on the numbers: some say $4.8 billion raised at a $48.7 billion valuation, others $5.55 billion at around $100 billion after the first day.

OpenAI is the anchor customer. It agreed in January to 750 megawatts of low-latency capacity, later widened to a deal worth about $20 billion through 2028, in three 250 MW tranches through Cerebras cloud. OpenAI also holds warrants worth up to 10 percent of Cerebras and loaned it $1 billion, per the S-1. A separate deal with AWS in March eased worries about customer concentration, though Cerebras has not said how much revenue comes from OpenAI.

item.title: Character.AI
item.description:
Character.AI lets people chat with custom characters, and about 20 million people use it each month. Its largest recent changes are about safety. It ended open-ended chat for users under 18 on November 25, 2025 and steers them toward Stories, a guided fiction format. Age checks can involve a selfie or ID. Reports say minors are about 10 percent of users.

In January 2026 Character.AI and Google agreed to settle several lawsuits over teen suicides and self-harm, including the case of Sewell Setzer, filed in Florida, Colorado, New York and Texas. Terms were not disclosed and neither company admitted liability. Kentucky’s attorney general filed the first state consumer action against the company on January 8, 2026. We did not confirm final court approval.

item.title: Cloudflare
item.description:
Cloudflare’s AI business has two sides: running AI and controlling who can scrape the web for it. On the first, Workers AI runs inference on Cloudflare’s network, reportedly including large open models like Kimi K2.5. In April 2026 the company announced Agent Cloud, with tools such as Dynamic Workers for sandboxing code that an AI writes. Agents Week 2026 brought around 30 announcements.

On the second, Cloudflare started blocking AI crawlers by default in 2025 and launched Pay Per Crawl so publishers could charge them. Reports say it is moving to a pay-per-use or pay-per-citation model, with You.com and Ceramic.ai among launch partners, though accounts differ on the details. One source says mixed-use AI crawlers are blocked by default from September 15, 2026 on pages with ads, and another headline says agents can now carry wallets to pay for access.

item.title: Codeium
item.description: Codeium made a free coding assistant and the Windsurf editor. Its path changed in 2025. Reports say Cognition closed a $250 million acquisition of Windsurf in December 2025, while one source says Google paid about $2.4 billion to license technology and hire its founders, and we could not reconcile the two. On June 2, 2026 Windsurf became Devin Desktop, the next generation of the editor, and windsurf.com now redirects to devin.ai/desktop.

item.title: Cohere
item.description:
Cohere sells language models to enterprises, with an emphasis on private deployment for banks, governments and other regulated customers. Command A is its flagship generation model, Embed and Rerank power search and retrieval, and North is its agent platform for employees, with a version aimed at pharmaceutical work.

In April 2026 Cohere announced it would merge with Germany’s Aleph Alpha, with Cohere’s shareholders holding about 90 percent of the combined company. Schwarz Group, an Aleph Alpha backer, said it would put $600 million into Cohere’s Series E. Later reports put the round at $2 billion to $3 billion, including money from the Canadian government, and one source gives a combined valuation near $20 billion. The deal needs antitrust approval, and we could not confirm it has closed.

item.title: Databricks
item.description:
Databricks sells a data platform and has turned it into an AI platform. Agent Bricks builds and evaluates agents on a company’s own data, Genie answers questions in plain language, and Lakebase, generally available since February 2026, is a serverless Postgres database meant for agent workloads. Databricks says Lakebase passed $100 million in run-rate revenue within months.

It also trains models, though less than before. MosaicML, acquired in 2023, produced DBRX and the MPT models, and Dolly was an early open instruction-tuned model. Today most customers use Databricks to run models from Anthropic, OpenAI and others against their own data.

item.title: Deepgram
item.description:
Deepgram builds speech-to-text and voice agent infrastructure. In January 2026 it raised $130 million in a Series C led by AVP at a $1.3 billion valuation and bought OfOne, a Y Combinator company doing voice AI for restaurant drive-thrus. Total funding estimates range from $215 million to $245 million. It also announced a partnership with IBM in February to bring voice AI to watsonx.

On the product side, Flux is its speech recognition model that handles interruptions in conversation, and Flux Multilingual reached general availability on April 29, 2026 in 10 languages. One source mentions a Flux TTS for real-time agents and annual recurring revenue above $100 million, without a date. Nova-3 is the main transcription model.

item.title: DeepSeek
item.description: DeepSeek is the Chinese lab that showed strong reasoning models could be trained and released openly for much less than Western labs spend. DeepSeek V4 previewed on April 24, 2026 in two versions. V4-Pro reportedly has about 1.6 trillion parameters with 49 billion active, and V4-Flash about 284 billion with 13 billion active. Both handle up to one million tokens of context. It is still labeled a preview, and DeepSeek has not given a date for the full release.

item.title: Descript
item.description:
Descript is an editor where you cut audio and video by editing the transcript. Its AI side is Underlord, an assistant that takes instructions such as removing filler words, finding highlights or building a short clip for social media. Underlord can remember your editing preferences across projects, and custom instructions let you set a house style once.

Descript has leaned on outside models for Underlord. Third-party coverage says it added Claude Sonnet 5, Fable 5 and Opus 5 during 2026, with Fable bringing video-aware editing, though we could not confirm those dates on Descript’s own pages. A public API entered open beta on May 14, 2026, so other tools can drive edits.

item.title: EleutherAI
item.description: EleutherAI is a nonprofit research collective that started the open language model movement with GPT-Neo, GPT-J and GPT-NeoX. Its Pythia suite, released in April 2023, has 16 models from 70 million to 12 billion parameters, built for studying how training shapes behavior. In June 2025 it released Common Pile v0.1, an 8 terabyte dataset of public domain and openly licensed text from 30 sources, with two 7B models, Comma v0.1-1T and 2T, trained on it to show that openly licensed data is enough for competitive models.

item.title: ElevenLabs
item.description:
ElevenLabs started with realistic text-to-speech and has widened into a voice platform. The newest models are Eleven v4 and v4 Turbo, released in October 2026. v4 aims for expressive, emotional speech, and Turbo targets real-time uses like voice agents with a median latency near 100 milliseconds. Both run in ElevenCreative, ElevenAgents and the API.

The agents product matters as much as the models now. Companies use it to build phone and chat agents that speak in a cloned or designed voice, and the company has pushed it into customer support. Dubbing, voice isolation and sound effects round out the creative side.

item.title: Figma
item.description:
Figma’s AI work centers on putting agents and generation tools inside the design canvas. At Config 2026 it announced Weave tools, more than 20 prebuilt AI workflows for jobs like background replacement and style transfer, free of AI credits during the open beta on Professional plans and above. Deeper integration between Figma and Weave is planned for later in the year.

The Figma Agent gained Skills, Connectors and Attachments so it can follow a team’s processes and pull context from other tools. Figma Motion, for animation, moved to open beta, and Code Layers lets designers work with real code on the canvas. Figma Make, which builds working prototypes from prompts, remains the main generative feature, though our sources said little about it.

item.title: GitHub
item.description:
GitHub’s AI work centers on Copilot, which began as inline code completion and now covers chat, code review and an agent that takes issues and opens pull requests. Copilot is sold as part of a GitHub subscription, with higher tiers for heavier use.

Agent HQ, announced at Universe in October 2025 and rolled out more widely in early 2026, changes the pitch. Instead of only offering Microsoft’s own agent, GitHub lets subscribers assign work to coding agents from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Cognition and xAI. A Mission Control view tracks what each agent is doing, and administrators choose which agents and models their teams can use. OpenAI’s Codex was the first outside agent to appear in it, followed by Claude Code.

item.title: Google
item.description:
Google’s AI is spread across the products people already use. Gemini is the assistant and the model family behind it, and Gemini 3.5 Flash became the default model after I/O in May 2026. Gemini Spark, a background agent that works inside Gmail and Docs, started with US Google AI Ultra subscribers. Google says AI Mode in Search passed 1 billion monthly users, and AI Overviews reach about 2.5 billion.

For developers, Google AI Studio and Vertex AI give access to the models through an API, and Antigravity 2.0 is a desktop app for running several coding agents at once. NotebookLM turns uploaded documents into a research assistant that can also produce audio summaries. Workspace has Gemini built into Docs, Sheets, and Gmail.

item.title: Google DeepMind
item.description: Google DeepMind is where Google’s frontier models get built. It formed in 2023 when DeepMind and Google Brain merged, and its main output is the Gemini family. Gemini 3.5 Flash shipped in May 2026 with a Pro model in testing at the time, and later releases include Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 4 Argon. Gemini Omni, announced at I/O, combines language reasoning with video generation and takes image, audio, video, and text as input.

item.title: Groq
item.description:
Groq makes the LPU, a chip built for fast inference that keeps model weights in on-chip SRAM instead of external memory. The company says this lets it generate tokens with far lower latency and, by its claim, about a tenth of the power of GPUs. GroqCloud sells access to open models running on that hardware through an API.

In December 2025, NVIDIA agreed to a non-exclusive license of Groq’s inference technology. Reports put the deal around $20 billion. It was not a full acquisition: founder Jonathan Ross and president Sunny Madra joined NVIDIA, while Groq stayed independent under CEO Simon Edwards and GroqCloud kept running. Commentators called it a reverse acquihire, a structure that avoids the antitrust review of a standard merger.

item.title: Huawei
item.description: Huawei’s AI role is mainly hardware. Its roadmap from September 2025 has the Ascend 950PR for prefill and recommendation in the first quarter of 2026, the 950DT for decode and training in the fourth quarter, and an Atlas 950 SuperPoD of up to 8,192 chips offering 8 exaflops at FP8. The Ascend 960 is set for 2027 and the 970 for 2028. A Digitimes report in March 2026 said the 950PR has nearly three times the performance of NVIDIA’s China-market H20, but we saw only the headline.

item.title: HubSpot
item.description:
HubSpot’s AI products come under the Breeze name. The company has sold Breeze agents for content, social, prospecting and customer support. In April 2026 it moved to outcome-based pricing for its agents, so customers pay when an agent completes the task. Agent actions are billed in HubSpot Credits, separate from seat licenses.

On July 23, 2026, according to one blog, HubSpot announced Agent Hub as a home for its agents, renamed Breeze Studio to Agent Builder and retired five beta agents. Reports differ on which model underlies the agents: one cites a developer changelog saying the default moved to GPT-5, another says GPT-4.x.

item.title: Hugging Face
item.description:
Hugging Face is where most open models get shared. Its Hub hosts well over a million models and several hundred thousand datasets, and the Transformers and Diffusers libraries are standard tooling for working with them. Most open-weight releases from other labs, including Qwen, Mistral and NVIDIA’s Nemotron, ship there first.

The company also trains its own models, mostly small ones. SmolLM and its successors target phones and laptops, StarCoder came out of the BigCode project, and smolagents is a lightweight library for building agents.

item.title: IBM
item.description:
IBM sells AI to large organizations, and the company says the point is governance and integration rather than the biggest model. Watsonx is the umbrella brand. Granite is the open model family, and Granite 4.0 introduced a hybrid Mamba and transformer design that IBM says cuts memory needs for long inputs by more than 70 percent. Granite models are released under Apache 2.0.

At Think 2026 in May, IBM positioned watsonx Orchestrate, now in private preview in its next-generation form, as a control plane for agents from any source, with shared policies. IBM Bob, an agentic development assistant, became generally available, and IBM Sovereign Core targets regulated customers that need to keep data in region. Reports also mention a Granite 4.2 release, which we could not confirm.

item.title: Ideogram
item.description:
Ideogram is known for rendering readable text inside generated images, a weakness in many rivals. It raised $22.3 million in seed funding in 2023 and $80 million in a Series A in February 2024 led by Andreessen Horowitz, and one 2026 analysis puts total funding just under $100 million. We found no new round in 2026.

One source reports Ideogram 4.0 launched as an open image model with weights on GitHub under ideogram-oss/ideogram4, but gives no date. A Fast Company piece in May 2026 on why Ideogram stands out came back as a headline only. Reviewers in early 2026 still recommend it when a prompt needs legible words, such as posters or logos.

item.title: Inflection AI
item.description:
Inflection AI made Pi, the conversational assistant, and in 2024 most of its founding team joined Microsoft, with Microsoft reportedly paying a $650 million licensing fee. Under CEO Sean White the company turned to enterprises with Inflection 3.0 models focused on emotional intelligence.

2026 reports conflict. One write-up cites a July 2026 VentureBeat report that Inflection is returning to consumers with Pi Journeys, and another capture dated July 22 says the enterprise page had been removed from its site. A third source still describes it as enterprise-focused. We could not read the original articles, so check inflection.ai. Pi continues to run.

item.title: Intel
item.description: Intel is behind NVIDIA and AMD in AI accelerators, and its own plans have shifted more than once. Gaudi 3 is still sold for training and inference through cloud partners, but reports say sales were weak and a planned successor, Falcon Shores, was cancelled for commercial release. The company’s current bet is Crescent Island, an inference-only data center GPU on the Xe3P architecture with 160 GB of LPDDR5X memory instead of HBM, which lowers cost at the expense of bandwidth.

item.title: Jasper
item.description:
Jasper sells AI for marketing teams and has repositioned from a writing tool to agents. Jasper Agents and Canvas launched in June 2025, and the company now says it offers over 100 specialized agents for jobs such as social planning, competitor research, content repurposing and email optimization. Jasper Grid, an orchestration layer for large content workflows, followed in early 2026.

On January 28, 2026 it published a State of AI in Marketing report from a survey of 1,400 marketers with Benchmarkit. It says 91 percent of teams now use AI, up from 63 percent in 2025, though only 41 percent can show ROI easily. A review described the 91 percent as daily use, which differs from the press release wording.

item.title: Kuaishou
item.description:
Kuaishou, the short-video platform, runs Kling, one of the strongest video generation models to come out of China. Kling 3.0 launched in February 2026 with video up to 15 seconds, up from 10, and inputs and outputs across text, images, audio and video. Turbo and native 4K output followed.

Kling is now a real business. Kuaishou reported Kling revenue over 650 million yuan in the first quarter of 2026, up more than 300 percent year on year, and over 850 million yuan in the second quarter, up more than 200 percent. It put annualized revenue at about $500 million in March. These figures are from Kuaishou’s earnings releases, which we read through news reproductions.

item.title: LangChain
item.description: LangChain sells the tools around agent building. The stack is layered: LangChain as the base framework, LangGraph for stateful agents, Deep Agents, an open-source agent harness launched in March 2026, and LangSmith for observability and evaluation, with Fleet running on LangSmith. In July 2026 it announced a collaboration with NVIDIA on a NemoClaw blueprint for Deep Agents. A package snapshot from October 4 listed langchain 1.4.3 and langgraph 1.2.12, and warned that AgentExecutor is deprecated, with migration needed before December 2026.

item.title: Leonardo AI
item.description:
Leonardo.Ai makes image generation tools for game art, product design and other creative work, built around its Phoenix model. Canva bought it in 2024, reportedly for about $320 million with roughly 120 staff, and Phoenix now runs Canva’s Dream Lab and Magic Media. A newsletter from August 2026 says Leonardo keeps operating independently and that Canva users’ content goes to Leonardo only if they opt in.

A September 2026 review lists Free, Essential at $12 a month, Premium at $30 and Ultimate at $60, with 150 fast tokens a day on the free tier. Most of the 2026 coverage is from review sites, not announcements, so confirm prices on the site.

item.title: Luma AI
item.description:
Luma AI began with 3D capture and now builds video and world models. Ray3, released in September 2025, is a reasoning video model that interprets a prompt before generating video, images and audio. Ray3.14, announced in January 2026, targeted animation, video-to-video and cinematic work. Dream Machine is the product people use.

In November 2025 Luma raised $900 million in a Series C led by Saudi Arabia’s Humain, with AMD Ventures, a16z, Amplify and Matrix, at a reported valuation near $4 billion. The money ties to Project Halo, a planned 2 gigawatt AI supercluster in Saudi Arabia where Luma will be an anchor customer. Luma says it wants to expand into simulation, design and robotics through world models.

item.title: Meta AI
item.description:
Meta changed direction on AI in 2026. Its Superintelligence Labs, led by Alexandr Wang, released Muse Spark in April, the first new frontier model since Llama 4 a year earlier. Unlike Llama, Muse Spark is closed. Artificial Analysis scored it 52 on its Intelligence Index, well above Llama 4 Maverick at 18. Meta says it hopes to open-source future versions but has not given a date.

Llama is still around. The Llama 3 and 4 models remain widely used by developers who want weights they can run themselves, and Meta has said it will keep supporting them. The Muse line now powers the Meta AI app, with versions for code and image generation, and reports describe a second model aimed at generating media.

item.title: Microsoft
item.description:
Microsoft’s AI business has two sides. Copilot is the assistant inside Windows, Microsoft 365, Edge and GitHub, and Azure AI is the cloud service that hosts models from OpenAI, Anthropic and others. Microsoft has been OpenAI’s largest outside backer since 2019.

In June 2026, around its Build conference, Microsoft AI under Mustafa Suleyman announced seven in-house MAI models. The flagship is MAI-Thinking-1, a reasoning model Microsoft says was trained without distilling from other companies’ models. The set also covers coding, image generation, speech and transcription. Suleyman described the effort as aimed at long-term self-sufficiency, which reads as hedging against dependence on OpenAI.

item.title: Midjourney
item.description:
Midjourney builds its own image models and has stayed independent of outside venture funding. V8 went to alpha testers on March 17, 2026. V8.1 became the default model on April 30, and one source says V8.2 followed as the default on July 24. V9 is in progress, and the public roadmap also mentions Niji 8 and a second video model.

Video is still on V1, launched in June 2025, which animates still images through the Animate button in the web editor. Sources disagree on video length and frame rate for the V8 era, with figures from 5 to 10 seconds, and some aggregator pages seem to label endpoints differently from Midjourney’s own names, so we do not give a spec here.

item.title: MiniMax
item.description:
MiniMax listed in Hong Kong in January 2026 and has been planning a second listing on Shanghai’s STAR Market, signing a tutoring agreement with CITIC Securities on May 29. Reports on its share performance conflict, ranging from a doubling on debut to a surge of over 1,600 percent, so we give no figure.

M3, launched on June 1, 2026, is an open-weight model for coding, agent work, long context and native multimodality, with a context window up to one million tokens, five times that of M2.7. MiniMax has not disclosed its size or training setup. A July analyst note expected upgrades in the second half focused on coding and agent post-training and on larger scale.

item.title: Mistral AI
item.description:
Mistral is the largest European model lab. It started with small open-weight models like Mistral 7B and Mixtral, and has since moved into commercial releases. Mistral Large 3, released in December 2025, is its most advanced language model, and the lineup also includes Codestral and Devstral for code, Pixtral for images and Voxtral for speech.

Le Chat is the consumer assistant, and Vibe, launched in May 2026, is a work and coding agent. Mistral sells to enterprises that want models running in their own data centers, which is where its open weights give it an edge over closed rivals.

item.title: Moonshot AI
item.description:
Moonshot AI makes Kimi, which first drew attention for long-context chat. Kimi K3, released in mid-July 2026, is an open-weight model with about 2.8 trillion parameters and a 1 million token context window. Moonshot published the weights and a technical report on Hugging Face on July 27.

Money followed. On July 29, 2026 it closed a $3.5 billion round at a $35 billion valuation, well above its original $1 to $2 billion target, with China’s National AI Industry Investment Fund among the leaders. One French report says annualized revenue passed $1 billion in August, up from $300 million two months earlier. Another source says Moonshot is weighing a Hong Kong listing and seeking NVIDIA Blackwell chips to train Kimi K4.

item.title: Notion
item.description: Notion’s AI went from a writing helper to agents that run on their own. Custom Agents arrived in Notion 3.3 on February 24, 2026. They work in the background on a schedule or when something happens, such as a new meeting note, and every run is logged so changes can be reviewed and reversed. They were free to try until May 3, 2026, and after that run on Notion credits sold as an add-on for Business and Enterprise plans.

item.title: Nous Research
item.description: Nous Research is known for the Hermes open models and, more recently, Hermes Agent. On October 7, 2026 it confirmed a $90 million Series B at a reported $1.5 billion valuation, bringing total funding to about $158 million. Reported investors include NVIDIA, Union Square Ventures, Menlo Ventures, Samsung and 1789 Capital. Nous has not itself confirmed the valuation. The round came with news of Hermes for Businesses, an enterprise product built on Hermes Agent, with no launch date or pricing.

item.title: NVIDIA
item.description: NVIDIA is best known for the GPUs that train and serve most large models, and the Vera Rubin platform shown at GTC in March 2026 is its next step. It combines seven chips, including the Vera CPU, Rubin GPU, NVLink 6 switch and a Groq-designed inference processor. NVIDIA’s own figures claim a large drop in cost per token compared with Blackwell, though those numbers come from the company and have not been independently tested.

item.title: OpenAI
item.description: OpenAI’s AI work centers on the GPT line and the products built on it. ChatGPT is the consumer face, and the API sells the same models to developers. The current generation is GPT-6, which ships in tiers named Luna, Sol, and Terra, with GPT-6.1 Sol and Terra following in the autumn of 2026. Reasoning models started with o1 and o3, and open-weight releases such as gpt-oss-20b and gpt-oss-120b let people run OpenAI models on their own hardware.

item.title: Oracle
item.description: Oracle’s AI business is mostly infrastructure. It is OpenAI’s partner for Stargate, with a July 2025 agreement for 4.5 gigawatts of data center capacity in the US. Active sites in Texas, New Mexico, Wisconsin and Michigan are under construction, and the Abilene, Texas flagship is designed to scale to 5 gigawatts. One source puts the OpenAI contract at $300 billion over five years, though figures vary, and reports in February 2026 said talks on a broader expansion had stalled while the core agreement held.

item.title: Otter.ai
item.description: Otter.ai transcribes meetings and is shifting toward agents. On October 20, 2026 it announced $320 million in non-dilutive growth financing from General Catalyst, with sources split on whether it came from the Customer Value Fund or the growth fund. It plans to use the money for enterprise customers, international expansion and agentic workflows. Recent products include Live Assist, a coaching agent for live calls, released in July 2026, and a new CMO joined in August.

item.title: Palantir Technologies
item.description:
Palantir’s AI product is AIP, the Artificial Intelligence Platform, which puts language models on top of a customer’s operational data in Foundry or Gotham and lets them take actions inside business systems. Customers range from hospitals and banks to defense agencies. For example, Customers Bank said on October 15, 2026 it would use Foundry and AIP for deposit onboarding.

The financial results show how much demand there is. Palantir’s Q3 2026 release raised full-year revenue guidance to about $8.53 billion, and its Q2 release put U.S. commercial revenue growth at 134 percent or more. We could not confirm the actual Q3 2026 figures from the sources we found.

item.title: Perplexity
item.description:
Perplexity runs an answer engine that cites its sources. It grew from search into a broader set of agent products. Comet is its AI browser, available free and using a mix of models including Perplexity’s own. Perplexity Computer, launched in February 2026, is a cloud agent that works on longer tasks, and Labs and Research modes produce reports and small apps.

For developers, the Sonar API is being replaced by a new Agent API, and Perplexity says it will support Sonar until September 27, 2026. New projects are told to start on the Agent API, which can route to models from other providers alongside Perplexity’s own.

item.title: Pika
item.description:
Pika builds consumer-friendly AI video tools. Pika 2.5, released in early 2026, added Scene Extension and Motion Control, which let you lengthen a clip or steer how things move. In April 2026 the company launched the beta of PikaStream 1.0, a real-time video model that powers a video chat skill for AI agents, so an agent can show up as a talking face.

AI Selves, announced in February 2026, is a different direction: digital twins with persistent memory that can post and chat on your behalf. It shows Pika moving away from competing only on clip quality against Runway, Google’s Veo and OpenAI’s Sora.

item.title: Poolside
item.description:
Poolside trains models for software engineering. Its Laguna family includes Laguna XS.2, a 33B model with 3B active released in April 2026, and Laguna M.1, a 225B model with 23B active, both reported as Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face. Its agent product and Malibu model name appear in aggregator pages, with Malibu as the flagship for complex engineering and Point for low-latency use.

The company’s finances had a setback in 2026. A planned $2 billion Series C at about $14 billion, with up to $1 billion from NVIDIA, reportedly collapsed in April after CoreWeave walked from a 15-year anchor lease for Project Horizon, its 2-gigawatt Texas data center plan. Another source gives $12 billion. Bloomberg reported on April 24 that NVIDIA would not lead a rescue, and Google talks over a 400 megawatt slice went quiet. One timeline gave cash runway through the third quarter of 2026. These come from aggregators citing Bloomberg, so check the originals.

item.title: Qualcomm
item.description:
Qualcomm’s AI business started in phones. Its Snapdragon chips include Hexagon NPUs that run assistants, camera features and translation on-device for most non-Apple flagship phones. AI Hub gives developers pre-optimized models for those chips.

In October 2025 Qualcomm announced a move into data centers with the AI200, due in 2026, and the AI250, due in 2027. The AI200 is a rack-scale inference system with 768 GB of LPDDR memory per card and liquid cooling. For the AI250 Qualcomm claims more than 10 times the effective memory bandwidth, using near-memory compute, but it has not published independent performance figures. Saudi Arabia’s Humain is the launch customer, with a planned 200 megawatt deployment.

item.title: Recraft
item.description: Recraft builds image generation for design work and is known for producing real vector graphics. Recraft V4, which the official docs date to February 2026, is a ground-up rebuild focused on design taste and prompt accuracy, in four versions: standard and Pro raster, plus vector. One aggregator gives May 7 instead, which we treat as less reliable. A V4.1 family followed, with one timeline listing May 14, a 2x speed-up on June 19 and price cuts on June 20.

item.title: Reka AI
item.description: Reka builds multimodal models that handle text, images, video and audio. Reka Flash is its flagship efficient model, with Core and Edge for larger and on-device use. The company raised $110 million in July 2025 from NVIDIA and Snowflake at a reported $1 billion valuation. A Reka news page also lists a $120 million round and a product called Nexus, but the snippet had no date, so we cannot place it.

item.title: Replit
item.description:
Replit lets people build apps from a prompt in the browser. Agent 4, launched in March 2026, is billed as ten times faster than Agent 3 and moves from a chat window to a canvas where you can also make spreadsheets, charts and games. It reached iPhone in May 2026 after a four-month dispute with Apple’s App Store review.

The company raised $400 million in a Series D led by Georgian on March 11, 2026, at a $9 billion valuation, three times its value six months earlier. Replit said it had more than 50 million registered users and 150,000 paying customers, and aims for $1 billion in annual revenue by the end of 2026. Revenue trackers differ on 2025 and 2026 figures, so treat those as estimates.

item.title: Runway
item.description:
Runway makes AI video generation and editing tools for filmmakers and studios. Its Gen models run from Gen-1 through Gen-4, and Gen-4.5 is the newest release we could confirm. One report says it topped the Artificial Analysis text-to-video leaderboard at launch, ahead of Google and OpenAI models. We found no announcement of a Gen-5 in the sources we checked.

The company’s attention has turned to world models, which simulate environments rather than just render clips. Runway shipped its first in December 2025 and has said a second will follow later in 2026. In February 2026 it raised $315 million in a Series E at a $5.3 billion valuation, backed by NVIDIA and AMD Ventures, with part of the money going to compute through CoreWeave.

item.title: Sakana AI
item.description:
Sakana AI is a Tokyo lab known for nature-inspired methods such as model merging and evolutionary search. Its AI Scientist, first shown in August 2024, automates research from idea to paper at about $15 per paper by the company’s estimate. Sakana and collaborators at the University of British Columbia, the Vector Institute and Oxford published the system in Nature on March 26, 2026.

It raised about $135 million (20 billion yen) in November 2025 at a post-money valuation near $2.65 billion, with MUFG and Khosla Ventures among the backers, which made it Japan’s most valuable startup. Google invested in January 2026, and a further strategic investment in March was undisclosed. Total funding figures differ by source, from $228 million to $379 million. Fugu is its commercial model line.

item.title: Salesforce
item.description:
Salesforce has bet its product line on Agentforce, its platform for AI agents that work inside CRM, Slack and Data Cloud. Dreamforce 2026 in September focused on getting agents into production. Salesforce announced seven job-specific agents, including Piper for inbound pipeline, which is generally available, and Hunter for outbound sales, due in November 2026. Agentforce Coworker reached 100,000 users in its first 35 days, according to the company.

A partnership with Anthropic moved to open beta at the event, bringing Claude into Salesforce and letting Salesforce data be used from inside Claude. Salesforce also showed its first in-house reasoning model during the keynote. Earlier research from Salesforce AI Research, including BLIP, CodeT5 and XGen, is still used in open-source work.

item.title: SambaNova Systems
item.description:
SambaNova makes its own AI chips and sells inference systems built around them. The SN50 chip arrived in February 2026 alongside a $350 million round led by Vista Equity Partners and Cambium Capital, and SambaNova says it beats NVIDIA’s B200 systems. General availability of SambaRack SN50 systems is expected in the second half of 2026, and SoftBank already deploys SN50.

Intel considered buying SambaNova for about $1.6 billion, but Bloomberg reported in January that talks collapsed. Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan is also SambaNova’s chairman and recused himself. The companies signed a multiyear partnership in February, under which SambaNova adopts Intel server chips and graphics cards, and sources disagree on how much Intel put into the round.

item.title: Samsung
item.description: Samsung’s AI shows up in three places: Galaxy phones, its own models and its chips. Galaxy AI covers features like live translation, photo editing and Circle to Search across phones, tablets and wearables. With the Galaxy S26 in February 2026, Samsung added Perplexity as a built-in system assistant with its own wake word, “Hey Plex”, next to Google Gemini and Bixby. Bixby uses Perplexity for more complex web questions while still handling actions on the phone.

item.title: SAP
item.description: SAP’s AI is Joule, an assistant built into its business applications, and at Sapphire 2026 in May it moved toward agents. The SAP Business AI Platform merges the Business Technology Platform, Business Data Cloud and Business AI into one governed environment, with a Knowledge Graph that gives agents access to a company’s business data and processes. Joule Studio 2.0 lets customers and partners build their own agents, with first availability from June 2026, and SAP set up a roughly 100 million euro fund for partners to build on it.

item.title: Scale AI
item.description: Scale AI sells training data, labeling and evaluation to AI labs and governments. Its biggest event came in June 2025, when Meta took a 49 percent stake for $14.3 billion and hired founder Alexandr Wang to lead its Superintelligence effort. In July 2025 Scale cut about 14 percent of its staff, around 200 roles, and ended contracts with 500 contractors. Interim CEO Jason Droege said the company had grown too fast.

item.title: SenseTime
item.description:
SenseTime started in computer vision and now sells large multimodal models. In the first half of 2026 it reported revenue of 2.91 billion yuan, up 23.4 percent, with recurring revenue of 1.14 billion yuan, and said it recorded its first profit in a half-year period. Full-year 2025 revenue passed 5 billion yuan, up 33 percent, with second-half EBITDA turning positive for the first time since its IPO.

Its model line is SenseNova. Releases listed in the H1 report include the NEO-Unify architecture, SenseNova U1 and U1.5, a Flash-Lite agent model for office work, a content model called U1-Pro and a spatial model, SI-8B. Sources disagree on whether U1-Pro had shipped and on whether the Flash-Lite version is 6.7 or 6.8. Seko, a video agent, produces about 10,000 minutes of video a day, and one report says it serves more than 800,000 creators and 1,300 enterprise clients.

item.title: ServiceNow
item.description: ServiceNow now sells AI under a few names. Now Assist is the generative layer inside its workflows. The Moveworks acquisition, announced at $2.85 billion and closed in December 2025, added conversational AI and enterprise search, and EmployeeWorks combines them with ServiceNow’s portal in early 2026. Autonomous Workforce uses teams of AI specialists with defined roles, such as a level-one service desk agent. ServiceNow says early internal results show it handling more than 90 percent of employee IT requests, a vendor-reported figure.

item.title: Shanghai AI Lab
item.description:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a state-backed research institute that publishes the InternLM language models and the InternVL multimodal models. Its newest confirmed release is Intern-S1-Pro, open-sourced on February 4, 2026. It is a 1-trillion-parameter scientific multimodal model built on the SAGE architecture, with a technical report on arXiv. The first Intern-S1 launched at the World AI Conference in July 2025.

One benchmark site claims a release in September 2026 but lists only one model with a date that conflicts with others, so we ignore it. The InternLM Hugging Face collection and GitHub organization are the places to check for anything newer.

item.title: Slack
item.description:
Slack’s AI work is Slackbot, which Salesforce rebuilt in 2026 from a simple helper into an agent. A new version launched in January, reportedly powered by Anthropic’s Claude, and on March 31 Salesforce announced more than 30 additional capabilities. Slackbot can answer questions, find information across channels, draft content, schedule meetings and act inside Slack, and it can send tasks to Agentforce agents.

It is included in Business+ and Enterprise+ plans without extra cost, a limited version arrived for free and Pro plans from April 2026, and Slack is to be bundled with every new Salesforce customer account from the summer. Slack’s model setup is reported to sit on a FedRAMP-certified model for government customers.

item.title: Snowflake
item.description:
Snowflake adds AI to the data warehouse through Cortex, a set of services that let customers run models and agents against data that never leaves their account. Cortex offers models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and Mistral, plus Snowflake’s own Arctic family.

Two partnerships define 2026. Snowflake and OpenAI announced a multi-year $200 million deal in February, putting OpenAI’s models natively inside Cortex across AWS, Azure and Google Cloud. A similar Anthropic deal, also reported at about $200 million, came first, and at Snowflake Summit in June 2026 the two said Claude was powering Cortex Code, a coding assistant. Snowflake is also a launch partner in Anthropic’s Claude Marketplace.

item.title: Stability AI
item.description:
Stability AI built its name on Stable Diffusion, the open image model that started the open generative image wave in 2022. The company has since shifted toward audio and music. In August 2026 it closed a $76 million Series B with Electronic Arts, Sony Music, Universal Music, Warner Music, AMD Ventures and others. The three music companies also licensed their catalogs for training.

That focus matches Stable Audio 3.0, which Stability says is trained only on licensed data. Reports disagree on whether it launched in May or June of 2026. Warner Music announced a collaboration with Stability earlier on tools for music creation that give artists control and pay them.

item.title: StepFun
item.description:
StepFun builds multimodal models for text, voice and video. Step 3.5 Flash came out in February 2026 under Apache 2.0, Step 3.7 Flash in May, and Step 5 Preview on September 18 with closed weights, a departure from the open releases before it.

The company has raised heavily and is preparing a Hong Kong IPO. It announced a Series B+ of over 5 billion yuan in January, and in May reportedly closed a $2.5 billion round while dismantling its offshore structure. One source says over 30 billion yuan, which conflicts. In June a report said it might file at a $12 billion valuation. We found no confirmation that the listing has happened.

item.title: Stripe
item.description:
Stripe’s AI efforts focus on how software agents pay for things. In September 2025 it launched the Agentic Commerce Protocol with OpenAI, and it later worked with Google, whose Universal Commerce Protocol Meta also joined. At Sessions in 2026 Stripe added the Machine Payments Protocol for billing agents over HTTP, along with a Link agent wallet, virtual cards for agents and x402 settlement in USDC stablecoin.

Stablecoins are central to the pitch. Stripe’s 2025 annual letter said stablecoin payment volume doubled to $40 billion, and co-founder John Collison predicts a torrent of agent-driven commerce. Observers note that actual agent spending is still small and the field is speculative.

item.title: Suno
item.description:
Suno generates full songs, with vocals, from a text prompt. The company settled with Warner Music Group in November 2025 and agreed to move to licensed models, which will replace its current ones in 2026. Warner’s artists decide whether their voices, names and compositions can be used, and Suno is buying Songkick from Warner.

A new model family, reported as v6, launched on September 9, 2026 with Warner, BMG and Believe. The version name is from a single source and we could not confirm it elsewhere. Suno reportedly raised a $400 million Series D in June 2026 at a $5.4 billion valuation, with about 2 million paid subscribers and $300 million in annual recurring revenue as of February, though these are secondary numbers.

item.title: Synthesia
item.description:
Synthesia makes AI avatar video for training and corporate communication. In January 2026 it closed a $200 million Series E at a $4 billion valuation, led by Google Ventures, with NVentures, Accel and Air Street Capital participating. Staff were able to sell shares in a secondary sale alongside it. Earlier rounds valued it at $2.1 billion in early 2025 and $1 billion in 2023.

Express-2 avatars have full-body gestures and are available on paid plans. Sources disagree on whether Express-2 launched in September 2025 or September 2026. Synthesia 3.0 added Video Agents, interactive videos that answer viewer questions in real time, per one summary. We found no further 2026 funding.

item.title: Technology Innovation Institute
item.description: The Technology Innovation Institute in Abu Dhabi makes the open Falcon models. On January 5, 2026 it released Falcon H1R 7B, a reasoning model built on a hybrid Transformer and Mamba design. TII says it matches or beats much larger reasoning models on math, code and general benchmarks. A fully FP8-quantized version followed on February 16 with the same benchmark results and lower memory use, according to the Falcon team’s own write-up.

item.title: Tencent
item.description:
Tencent’s models carry the Hunyuan name, and its consumer assistant is Yuanbao. The current flagship is Hy3, launched on July 6, 2026 after an open-sourced preview in April. It is a mixture-of-experts model with 295 billion total parameters, about 21 billion active, under Apache 2.0, with three reasoning modes. One source lists a 256K token context window.

Tencent rebuilt the Hunyuan line in 2026 under chief AI scientist Yao Shunyu, a former OpenAI researcher, and Hy3 was the first major result. It was put straight into Yuanbao and into Tencent’s coding and work tools, including CodeBuddy and WorkBuddy, and developer pricing was cut at the same time. WeChat, Tencent’s messaging app, is the obvious distribution channel for whatever comes next.

item.title: Tenstorrent
item.description: Tenstorrent, led by chip architect Jim Keller, builds AI processors on the open RISC-V standard. Its Blackhole chip sits inside Galaxy servers with 32 chips each. Sales opened in April 2026 and volume shipping was announced in May. In a June interview, Keller said it was producing 1,000 Galaxy servers with about half already sold, though that is his claim relayed by a Taiwanese outlet. An April analysis said the software stack was still early for Blackhole.

item.title: Together AI
item.description:
Together AI is a cloud for running open models. Developers use it to call models such as Llama, Qwen and DeepSeek through an API, to fine-tune them, or to rent GPU clusters. It also published RedPajama, an early open training dataset and model set.

The company raised an $800 million Series C led by Aramco Ventures, reported on July 1, 2026, at an $8.3 billion valuation. It says it plans to scale capacity roughly fifty times over five years. Partnerships include a multi-year deal to run inference on IBM Cloud with NVIDIA B300 systems, a strategic deal with Humain in Saudi Arabia and an Inference Exchange with Equinix and NVIDIA, expected in early 2027. A job posting put the IBM deal at $240 million, which we could not confirm.

item.title: Twilio
item.description:
Twilio’s AI work is about voice and messaging agents. ConversationRelay, generally available since May 2025, lets developers connect any language model to a phone call with streaming speech. Its insights feature, which reports latency, interruptions and handling time, reached general availability on May 6, 2026. Twilio’s changelog also lists Deepgram’s Flux speech-to-text model for turn detection and PCI-compliant voice workflows.

At SIGNAL 2026 Twilio presented a “Conversation Layer” over voice, SMS, WhatsApp and RCS that adds context, memory and orchestration for agents. One blog says the HIPAA and PCI support could open regulated industries, though we found only one source for the full product list.

item.title: Udio
item.description: Udio was founded by former DeepMind researchers to turn prompts into songs. In October 2025 it settled its lawsuit with Universal Music Group and agreed to build a licensed platform, trained only on authorized music on an opt-in basis, as a subscription where users can customize, stream and share songs inside a protected space. Artists are to be paid both for training use and when fans generate music from their work. The platform was set for 2026, with no firm date, and we found no report that it has launched. The existing product stays up in a restricted form during the transition, with fingerprinting and filtering in place.

item.title: Upstage
item.description:
Upstage, in Seoul, makes the Solar models and document AI. Solar Pro 3, released in March 2026, is a 102-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model focused on agents, tool calling and coding. It is one of the national champions in South Korea’s sovereign AI foundation model program, whose first output was Solar Open 100B in January 2026. A plagiarism dispute followed that release.

AMD and Upstage expanded their collaboration on March 18, 2026, and on May 3 a government-backed fund approved a $400 million direct equity investment, though one analysis’s breakdown could not be verified. Sources disagree on Solar Pro 4. One calls it the new flagship reasoning model, another says it was released in August 2026, and a third says it was planned for late July, so the timing is unconfirmed.

item.title: Vercel
item.description: Vercel is a platform for web developers that has pushed hard into AI tooling. The AI SDK, an open-source TypeScript library, reached version 7 around late June 2026, and Vercel says it has a harness layer for running agents. AI Gateway gives a single endpoint for many models with fallback and spend tracking, and new models appear there quickly. In June 2026 its changelog noted Claude Fable 5 access was suspended there while other Anthropic models stayed available.

item.title: Voyage AI
item.description: Voyage AI makes embedding and reranking models for retrieval, and MongoDB acquired it in 2025 to put vector search inside its database. On January 15, 2026 MongoDB announced the Voyage 4 family: voyage-4, the flagship voyage-4-large, voyage-4-lite for cost and latency, and an open-weights voyage-4-nano for local use. MongoDB says the series beats Gemini and Cohere on the public RTEB leaderboard, and that voyage-4-large improves retrieval F1 by 3.7 percent over the nearest competitor. Those are vendor claims.

item.title: Workday
item.description:
Workday’s AI is built around agents for HR and finance. In September 2025 it agreed to buy Sana, a Swedish AI company, for about $1.1 billion, adding Sana Agents and an agent builder with search. Workday called the aim becoming the “front door for work.” It had already bought Paradox for recruiting and Flowise, a low-code agent builder, in 2025.

The company also set up an Agent System of Record, where customers can register and manage agents, including those built in Microsoft’s Azure AI Foundry and Copilot Studio. Illuminate is the brand for its AI features in recruiting, payroll and planning.

item.title: Writer
item.description: Writer sells a full-stack AI platform to large companies and trains its own Palmyra models. Palmyra X5, released in April 2025, is an adaptive reasoning model with a 1 million token context window, available on Writer’s platform and Amazon Bedrock. Writer says it was trained mostly on synthetic data for about $1 million in GPU costs, a claim from the company. AI HQ is the hub where enterprises build, run and supervise agents on those models, and early use cases include financial reporting, RFP responses and support documentation.

item.title: xAI
item.description:
xAI makes Grok, the chatbot that lives inside X and also runs as a standalone app and API. The company was founded by Elon Musk in 2023, and SpaceX acquired it in February 2026. The two were fully merged by May, and the work now sits under a SpaceXAI division.

Grok 4.5, released on July 8, 2026 alongside a partnership with Cursor, is the newest model we could confirm. It targets coding and agent use. Other sources mention a Grok 4.6, but we found only one report of it. Grok 5 is reported to be in training on Colossus 2, a cluster SpaceX puts at roughly one gigawatt of combined draw with the original Colossus.

item.title: Zapier
item.description:
Zapier connects apps, and its AI work is mostly about letting agents use those connections. Zapier MCP, built on the Model Context Protocol and adopted in September 2025, lets assistants such as Claude call actions across thousands of apps with a couple of clicks. Third-party coverage cites anywhere from 8,000 to over 9,000 apps depending on date.

Zapier Agents moved from chat-style helpers toward automation-first agents that run and orchestrate Zaps, and are now generally available with enterprise MCP support. An SDK in open beta since April 2026 reportedly lets agents make arbitrary API calls to about 10,000 apps. Enterprise customers can now apply one policy layer to no-code workflows, agents and MCP-connected assistants.

item.title: Zhipu AI
item.description: Zhipu AI, which trades its products as Z.ai, became the first foundation model company listed on the Hong Kong exchange, on January 8, 2026 (ticker 2513.HK), raising about HK$4.35 billion at HK$116.20 a share. It builds the GLM models. GLM-5, reported at 744 billion parameters, was released as open source in mid-February 2026, aimed at agents and complex engineering tasks. GLM-5.2 followed on June 17 and one source ranks it second on Code Arena’s front-end benchmark, behind Claude Fable 5.

item.title: Zoom
item.description: Zoom’s AI is AI Companion, now at version 3.0. It summarizes meetings, drafts replies and, since March 2026, builds custom agents and AI-first Docs, Sheets and Slides. Zoom calls its approach federated: tasks go to its own small and large models or to third-party models from OpenAI and Anthropic, and users can reach open models such as NVIDIA’s Nemotron. Zoom claims this combination beat OpenAI and Google on one hard benchmark, which we did not verify.
